import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import SpectralClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Compute t-statistics for all features
    t_stats = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx])
        y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx])
        t_stat = (y1_mean - y0_mean) / (np.std(feats.x[:, col_idx]) + 1e-8)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Find top features by t-statistic
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1]
    top_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in sorted_indices[:5]]
    
    # Check for strong correlations to identify potential modules
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    np.fill_diagonal(corr_matrix, 0)
    
    # Look for highly correlated pairs
    high_corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                high_corr_pairs.append((i, j))
    
    # If we have strong correlations, try to form a simple module
    if len(high_corr_pairs) > 0:
        # Simple approach: take top 3 features with highest t-stats
        # that also have strong correlations with others
        module_features = top_features[:3]
        
        # Compute weighted score using t-statistics
        weights = []
        for fid in module_features:
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx])
            y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx])
            t_stat = (y1_mean - y0_mean) / (np.std(feats.x[:, col_idx]) + 1e-8)
            weights.append(abs(t_stat))
        
        # Normalize weights
        weights = np.array(weights)
        weights = weights / (np.sum(weights) + 1e-8)
        loadings = dict(zip(module_features, weights))
        
        return Design(
            drivers=tuple([module_features[0]]),
            columns=tuple(module_features),
            products=(),
            loadings=loadings
        )
    
    # If no strong correlations, just use top features
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple([top_features[0]]),
        columns=tuple(top_features),
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
